title: The slice-site open extension is recovered from its closure
statement: Let X be any topological space, U an open subset, F an abelian sheaf, and G the sheafification of the slice-site extension-by-zero presheaf of F.over U [def-weil-pbc-site-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Let i:closure(U)→X be the inclusion. The inverse-image adjunction unit G→i_*i^{-1}G [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 02UZ, first paragraph: closure-support observation; Sheaves Lemma 00AE

proof.text: Outside U every neighbourhood V has no inclusion V→U, so every section of the extension presheaf is zero. Represent each stalk element by a germ; it is zero. The sheafification unit is a stalk isomorphism, so the sheafified stalk is zero outside U and therefore outside closure(U).

Put F′=i^{-1}G. Outside closure(U), both stalks of the unit are zero, by the preceding calculation and the closed-pushforward zero-stalk formula. On the closure, compose the unit stalk map with the closed-pushforward germ comparison. The resulting map equals the inverse-image stalk isomorphism: apply the germ formula of both maps, and then stalk hom extensionality. Since the latter two maps are isomorphisms, the unit stalk map is an isomorphism.
Apply the generic stalkwise isomorphism criterion (directly in AddCommGrpCat) to the unit of abelian sheaves.
